LMGTE.title: AF Corse’s #55 Ferrari holds off its stablemate for the Paul Ricard win
LMGTE.dek: Griffin, Rugolo and Cameron won LMGTE for AF Corse, a Ferrari sweep of the top five, after pole-sitting SMP slipped to seventh and Gulf’s new Porsche faded from the lead.

facts.v: Bertolini’s 1:55.691 in the SMP Ferrari was his third LMGTE pole of 2014, 0.196s clear of Piccini’s Kessel car.

chapters.title: A three-point lead and a new Porsche
text: Matt Griffin and Duncan Cameron arrived at Paul Ricard leading the LMGTE standings by three points after wins at Silverstone and the Red Bull Ring. Michele Rugolo rejoined them in the AF Corse #55 Ferrari, though he could not win the title after missing Imola for the Mille Miglia. Second in the table were the SMP Racing trio of Andrea Bertolini, Sergey Zlobin and Viktor Shaitar in the #72 Ferrari.

The big talking point was the Gulf Racing UK Porsche 911 RSR, a new 991-based car making its series debut after 800km of testing at Estoril. The ACO changed the Balance of Performance for the Porsche and Aston Martin entries, adding 5kg to the 911 RSR and cutting 20kg from the older 997 cars. Kessel Racing was back to two Ferraris, and James Walker rejoined JMW for the weekend.

Practice underlined Ferrari’s straight-line strength. The #55 led the first session, Bertolini topped the second on 1:55.913, and Gulf’s Aston Martin lost most of the afternoon with an engine problem.

chapters.title: Bertolini’s third pole of the year
text: Bertolini put the #72 SMP Ferrari on LMGTE pole with a 1:55.691, his third of the season. Giacomo Piccini was 0.196s behind in the #80 Kessel Ferrari, with Griffin’s #55 third on 1:55.911.

Adam Carroll was fourth in the new Gulf Porsche #86 on 1:56.010, an encouraging start for a car that had needed hard graft to be ready. The #54 AF Corse and JMW’s #66 Ferrari were fifth and sixth. Gulf’s Aston Martin #85 managed a single lap after its engine change and was last in class on 2:04.550.

chapters.title: Barker takes the Porsche to the front
text: Benjamin Barker started the Gulf Porsche from fourth and raced into a comfortable lead, showing the pace of the new 911 RSR. Behind him Cameron’s opening stint in the #55 kept the class leaders honest, while Daniel McKenzie drove the first two hours for JMW’s #66.

chapters.title: The Ferraris reel in the Porsche
text: The Porsche could not hold its advantage once Michael Wainwright took over. The lead passed to the AF Corse-run Ferraris. Griffin duelled with Mirko Venturi in the AT Racing #56 before Rugolo took over.

chapters.title: Rugolo resists Kaffer
text: Pierre Kaffer closed on Rugolo in the final hour in the #56 AT Racing Ferrari, but the #55 stayed in front to take the win. JMW’s #66, with Walker finishing the job, completed the podium. Kessel’s #80 and the AF Corse #54 took fourth and fifth, giving Ferrari the top five.

chapters.title: AF Corse extend their lead
text: The #55 won on 119 laps, with the #56 and #66 on the same lap. The #54 and #80 were fourth and fifth, also on the lead lap. Gulf’s Porsche #86 and the pole-sitting #72 were sixth and seventh, a lap down, followed by IMSA Performance Matmut’s Porsche #76. Kessel’s #81 was ninth, two laps behind, then the Aston Martin #85 and the Porsche #67. The #70 and #58 were not classified. Bertolini set the class fastest lap, 1:56.735.

It was the #55’s second win in a row and third of the season. Griffin called it the toughest race of their year, and Rugolo said the crew would approach Estoril the same way, only with more caution. With SMP’s #72 back in seventh, the AF Corse crew's lead grew before the finale at Estoril on 18–19 October.

GTC.title: SMP’s #73 Ferrari takes its first GTC win of 2014 after three seconds
GTC.dek: Beretta, Markozov and Ladygin beat the Formula Racing Ferrari after starting eleventh in class, while ART’s McLaren took third ahead of the pole-sitting SMP.

facts.v: The #73 crew had finished runner-up at each of the first three rounds before taking this victory.

chapters.title: SMP lead a deep GTC field
text: GTC arrived at Paul Ricard with SMP Racing’s #73 Ferrari of Olivier Beretta, David Markozov and Anton Ladygin in front of the standings, on the back of three runner-up finishes. The AF Corse-run Formula Racing Ferrari of Johnny Laursen, Mikkel Mac and Jan Magnussen was second in points, with SMP’s #71 crew, winners at the Red Bull Ring, third.

Team Ombra made its ELMS debut with Mario Cordoni and Marco Zanuttini in a Ferrari, while the ART Grand Prix McLarens and the Team Russia by Barwell BMW were expected to feature. The ACO enlarged the air restrictor on the Porsche 911 GT3 R from 56mm to 60mm.

SMP filled the top three in the first practice, with Luca Persiani fastest on 1:59.140. Mike Parisy then led the second session for Prospeed Competition on 1:58.452 in the Porsche, just two tenths clear of the #71.

chapters.title: Persiani on pole, Korjus close
text: Persiani took pole for the #71 SMP Ferrari with a 1:57.336, his second of the season. Kevin Korjus was 0.177s behind in the #98 ART McLaren despite meeting traffic late in his lap. The second row was the #95 AF Corse Ferrari of Cedric Sbirrazzuoli (1:57.745) and Jonathan Cocker’s Team Russia by Barwell BMW on 1:57.891.

Markozov made a mistake on his lap, leaving the eventual winners eleventh on the class grid. The back of the field was more than two seconds off the pace, with the AF Corse #63, Ombra and Sofrev-ASP cars all slower than 2:00.9.

chapters.title: Ladygin starts the climb
text: Anton Ladygin started the #73 from eleventh in class and worked forward lap by lap. Once he had cleared the pack he came under pressure from the Formula Racing Ferrari, particularly when Magnussen and then Mac were at the wheel, and Markozov soaked up that pressure in his stints.

chapters.title: Korjus moves up
text: Pole-sitting SMP had a difficult afternoon, with the #71 and the #57 both losing time. Korjus took over the running of the #98 McLaren and hunted down the #95 AF Corse Ferrari late on, making a bold move to take third place.

chapters.title: Beretta’s crew home first
text: The #73 finished on 117 laps to win, with the Formula Racing Ferrari #60 second on the same lap. Korjus’s ART McLaren denied SMP a double podium by finishing third, a lap behind, ahead of the #71 and the #95.

chapters.title: A first win and a bigger lead
text: The #73 won GTC, with the #60 second on the same lap and the #98 third, a lap down. The #71 was fourth ahead of the #95 and the AF Corse #94, then the Porsche #93 of Pro GT by Almeras, the McLaren #99 in eighth and Prospeed’s Porsche #75 in ninth. The BMW #78 was tenth and SMP’s #57 eleventh, with the #63 and #59 three laps down and Ombra’s #92 five behind at the back. Mediani set the class fastest lap, 1:58.805.

It was SMP’s second GTC win in a row, although this time it came from the #73 rather than the #71. Beretta said the start was good, the strategy worked and the car stayed out of trouble. The result extended the trio’s title lead going into the finale at Estoril on 18–19 October.
